title: Don't rely on deeds
hook: a sign of relying on your deeds is losing hope when you slip (Hikam 1, paraphrased)
tomorrow: why would a seed choose to stay buried in the dark?

segments.voice: Yesterday, The Hikam opened: wisdoms, small ones, one at a time. Today, the very first one, and a week to hold up beside it.

One bad grade, one rejected pitch, one sharp comment from someone you respect, and suddenly it's all over: every plan, every hope, gone in an afternoon. The spiral is fast and very convincing. It feels like seeing clearly at last. What does a crash like that actually reveal? Ibn Ata'illah opens the Hikam with exactly this. Among the signs that you're relying on your deeds, he says, is losing hope when you slip.
screen: `ONE BAD GRADE, ALL HOPE GONE.` → `WHAT DOES THE CRASH REVEAL?` → `THE FIRST APHORISM.`

segments.voice: The crash shows where your weight was. If your hope collapses at one slip, it was resting on your record, and records wobble. He isn't saying deeds don't matter; the whole book assumes you'll keep doing good. He's asking what you lean on. A hadith in al-Bukhari makes the same turn. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said no one will enter Paradise by their deeds alone. Not even you? his companions asked. Not even me, he said, unless God covers me with his mercy. So you keep working, and you lean on mercy. Now, hold up the week beside that first saying. Stillness making room in prayer: the heart of prayer. A fast that reaches the eyes and tongue: the fast of the heart. A fogged glass that isn't broken: the mirror. One steady hand, one open: two halves. A last book that sorts the day: preparing to meet him. A small book read slowly: wisdoms. Every one of those is a practice, and every one could become a new record to lean on. Ibn Ata'illah's first word guards against exactly that. Do them all. Rest on none of them.
screen: `THE CRASH SHOWS YOUR WEIGHT.` · `NOT EVEN ME, UNLESS MERCY.` · `A WEEK, HELD UP.` · `DO THEM ALL, REST ON NONE.` · then, large: `RELY ON HIM.`

segments.voice: Sit back and let the chair take your whole weight: shoulders, arms, legs, nothing held up by effort. Rest your hands palms up. For the sit, notice what it's like to be fully held without earning it.
screen: `LET THE CHAIR TAKE YOUR WEIGHT.` · `HELD, WITHOUT EARNING IT.`

segments.voice: Don't rely on deeds. The Hikam's first saying: losing all hope at a slip shows what you were leaning on. Keep doing good; lean on God.
Rely on him: keep working hard, and let mercy hold the weight you were carrying alone. Two weeks, closed.

fork.setup: your friend has prayed on time for a whole month, then misses one and says she's ruined everything and might as well stop. what fits the first aphorism?
options: agree the streak is broken, so she should start over from zero tomorrow.
tell her the missed prayer cancels out the month, so she'd better double up.
the crash shows she was leaning on her streak; keep praying, and lean on mercy.
fork.reveal: losing all hope at one slip is the sign Ibn Ata'illah names. the fix isn't to stop doing good; it's to stop resting on the record.
